articleTitle: Low latency video communications over high bandwidth-delay networks using FEC
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Time Critical Data Communications
abstract: Discusses sources of delay for real-time video data transmitted through packet-switched networks. We describe an experiment in which we investigate the use of forward error correction (FEC) as a means of controlling errors during the transport of coded video data. We compare this with traditional ARQ error control techniques. We conclude that for high bandwidth-delay networks, FEC could provide a suitable means of controlling errors in real-time video data.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: TCCA and QoS (time-critical communications architectures and quality of service)
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Time Critical Data Communications
abstract: Initiatives to identify user requirements for time-critical communications architectures (TCCA) and for quality of service (QoS) have led to standardisation work that will be widely applicable. The concepts and mechanisms which are described have relevance across almost all application areas. Eventually, OSI systems will be able to be selected for their performance as well as for their functionality, and their operational behaviour will be able to be monitored and tuned to meet the precise requirements of their users.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: The integration of real-time interactive speech with data on local area network (LANs)-a step towards "multi-media" in a commercial industrial environment
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Time Critical Data Communications
abstract: Research at the author's university has identified that communication between users of workstations in an environment would be considerably enhanced if a real-time speech link was available in addition to 'screen-share' facilities. This paper investigates the problems of implementing a real-time interactive speech link by integrating the speech packets (PCM) within the data frames employed on commercially available LANs. This is a step towards remote tutoring in higher education.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>
